# source: conformance/scenarios/directories.txt

scenario directories/trailing-slash-matches-only-directories
kind normative
spec If there is a separator at the end of the pattern then the pattern will only match directories, otherwise the pattern can match both files and directories.
file .gitignore
| build/
path build/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build/
path build => NONE
path src/build/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build/
path src/build => NONE
path build/a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build/
path build/a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build/
path src/build/a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build/

scenario directories/no-slash-matches-file-and-directory
kind normative
spec Otherwise the pattern can match both files and directories.
file .gitignore
| build
path build/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build
path build => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build
path src/build/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build
path src/build => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build
path build/a => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:build

scenario directories/ignored-directory-contents
kind normative
spec Git does not list the contents of an excluded directory, so everything beneath an ignored directory is ignored.
file .gitignore
| vendor/
path vendor/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:vendor/
path vendor/lib.c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:vendor/
path vendor/a/b/c.c => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:vendor/
path vendor/a/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:vendor/
path vendor/.hidden => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:vendor/
path vendors/lib.c => NONE

scenario directories/wildcard-with-trailing-slash
kind normative
spec For example, a pattern "doc/frotz/" matches "doc/frotz" directory, but not "a/doc/frotz" directory.
file .gitignore
| doc/frotz/
| *.d/
path doc/frotz/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:doc/frotz/
path doc/frotz => NONE
path a/doc/frotz/ => NONE
path x.d/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:*.d/
path x.d => NONE
path a/x.d/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:*.d/
path x.d/file => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:*.d/
path x.dd/ => NONE

scenario directories/trailing-slash-pattern-on-file-named-like-dir
kind normative
spec A pattern ending in a slash never matches a regular file.
file .gitignore
| log/
path log => NONE
path a/log => NONE
path log/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:log/
path a/log/ => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:log/

scenario directories/pattern-with-double-trailing-slash
kind git-quirk
spec Behavior of a pattern ending in several slashes is not described by gitignore(5).
note Git strips only the final slash and then compares the remainder, so the extra slash keeps the pattern from matching.
file .gitignore
| a//
| b//c
path a/ => NONE
path b/c => NONE
path b/c/ => NONE
path b/ => NONE
